questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.7]\draw (-2,-1.4)--(2,1.4);\draw (-2,1.4)--(2,-1.4);\draw (0.42,0.3) arc[start angle=35,end angle=145,radius=0.52];\draw (-0.42,-0.3) arc[start angle=215,end angle=325,radius=0.52];\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Which relationship describes the marked pair?

options.why: Chooses angles across the vertex even though they share no arm.
Infers a $90$ degree total without any angle measures.
Infers a $180$ degree total without any angle measures.

questions.solution_text:
The marked angles are opposite each other where two straight lines intersect.
They are vertically opposite.

options.why: Uses a total of $180$ degrees, identifying a supplementary angle.
Assumes equal measures automatically form a complementary pair.
Subtracts from $100$ instead of from $90$ degrees.
Finds the difference $112 - 90$ instead of subtracting $112$ from $180$.
Subtracts from $190$ instead of from $180$ degrees.
Assumes equal measures automatically form a supplementary pair.

options.text: Yes, because they share vertex $V$ and arm $VR$.
options.why: Checks the common vertex and arm but ignores that adjacent angles must not overlap.

options.text: No, because they have different vertices.
options.why: Misidentifies the vertex; both angles have vertex $V$.

options.text: Yes, because any two angles with the same vertex are adjacent.
options.why: Uses a common vertex alone and ignores the common-arm and non-overlap requirements.

questions.solution_text:
Both angles share vertex $V$ and arm $VR$.
However, $\angle QVR$ lies inside $\angle PVR$, so they overlap.
They are not adjacent.
